In mathematics, especially in [[category theory]], a '''balanced category''' is a [[category (mathematics)|category]] in which every bimorphism (a morphism that is both a [[monomorphism]] and [[epimorphism]]) is an [[isomorphism]].

The [[category of topological spaces]] is not balanced (since continuous bijections are not necessarily homeomorphisms), while a topos is balanced.<ref>{{harvnb|Johnstone|1977}} <!-- I don’t have the book so I don’t know the exact location --></ref> This is one of the reasons why a topos is said to be nicer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://golem.ph.utexas.edu/category/2014/04/on_a_topological_topos.html|title=On a Topological Topos at The n-Category Café|website=golem.ph.utexas.edu}}</ref>

== Examples ==
The following categories are balanced:
*'''Set''', the [[category of sets]].
*'''Grp''', the [[category of groups]].
*An [[abelian category]].<ref>§ 2.1. in Sandro M. Roch, [https://page.math.tu-berlin.de/~roch/files/abelian_categories.pdf A brief introduction to abelian categories], 2020</ref>
*'''CHaus''', the category of [[Compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] spaces (since a continuous bijection there is homeomorphic).

An [[additive category]] may not be balanced.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathoverflow.net/questions/119821/is-an-additive-category-a-balanced-category|title=Is an additive category a balanced category?|website=MathOverflow}}</ref> Contrary to what one might expect, a balanced [[pre-abelian category]] may not be abelian.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathoverflow.net/questions/41722/is-every-balanced-pre-abelian-category-abelian|title=Is every balanced pre-abelian category abelian?|website=MathOverflow}}</ref>

A [[quasitopos]] is similar to a topos but may not be balanced.
